title: Zariski pullback covers and zero detection on localized module sites
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $T_\tau$ be either its small etale site or its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with small representatives and a common coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ be a set-indexed Zariski open cover of $T$. The family $(U_i\to T)$ is a covering of $T_\tau$. For every object $V\to T$ of $T_\tau$, the family $(V\times_T U_i\to V)$ is a covering in $T_\tau$, in the small site $V_\tau$, and in the localized site $T_\tau/V$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Let $\mathcal O$ be any sheaf of commutative rings on $T_\tau$, and let $F$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $s_iF$ for the sectionwise restriction to $T_\tau/U_i$, a sheaf of $\mathcal O|_{U_i}$-modules, so $s_iF(W\to U_i)=F(W)$. The restriction map
$$ F(V)\longrightarrow\prod_{i\in I}F(V\times_T U_i) $$
is injective for every $V\to T$. In particular,
$$ F=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad s_iF=0\text{ for every }i\in I. $$
Here $F=0$ means that $F$ is a zero object in the module-sheaf category, equivalently every section module $F(V)$ is zero. If $T=\varnothing$, the empty family covers every object of $T_\tau$, every module sheaf on $T_\tau$ is zero, and the equivalence includes $I=\varnothing$. No quasi-compactness, finiteness of the covering, constant-coefficient hypothesis or existence of points of the topos is required.

proof.text: For any scheme $S$ and Zariski open cover $(W_i)$ of $S$, each inclusion $W_i\hookrightarrow S$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. Their images cover $S$, so [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] makes this an etale covering. Since the inclusions are etale and jointly surjective, [lem-pur-etale-proetale-cover] (Stacks 098B) makes the same family a pro-etale covering in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], i.e. with the required finite affine refinements; joint surjectivity alone is not substituted for that condition. Apply this with $S=T$ and $W_i=U_i$.

Fix v:V→T and use the inverse-image opens W_i=v⁻¹(U_i), which cover V.left since the U_i cover T. Their inclusions are open immersions and hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. Apply the joint-surjectivity criterion of [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] directly to the morphisms W_i→V in T.Etale and to W_i→V.left in V.left.Etale. For the pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], its precoverage is the comap of the scheme precoverage, so apply [lem-pur-etale-proetale-cover] to these same etale open inclusions. This proves the covering assertions without constructing chosen categorical pullbacks or invoking an additional base-change theorem. The inverse-image open representatives are already the objects in the Lean statement. Finally the topology on the slice from [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] tests the underlying sieve: Sieve.overEquiv_ofArrows identifies it with the covering just proved.

proof.text: The underlying abelian presheaf of F is a sheaf by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use Mathlib Presheaf.IsSheaf.isSeparated for the covering sieve generated by the inverse-image open inclusions from Steps 1-2. Every arrow of this sieve factors as b followed by a covering inclusion; functoriality of restrictions carries equality on each covering member to equality on that arrow. Separatedness then gives x=y, which proves injectivity without points, constant coefficients, or finiteness assumptions.

source.place: Tag 00VM, definition-sheaf-sets and equation-sheaf-condition; Tag 00VR, definition-sheaf

proof.text: First prove from [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] that IsZero F is equivalent to singleton section modules: evaluate id_F=0 at each object and use ModuleCat.isZero_iff_subsingleton; conversely singleton sections force all components of id_F to equal zero. By [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], F.over A evaluated at W→A has the same section module F(W), definitionally. For the backward local-zero implication pull the covering sieve of T back along V→T using GrothendieckTopology.pullback_stable. Each arrow W→V in this sieve factors through some U_i, so F.over U_i being zero forces F(W) to be a singleton. Separatedness now forces F(V) to be a singleton, and the sectionwise criterion gives IsZero F. Conversely global singleton sections remain singleton under the sectionwise restriction formula. This is a generic ringed-site argument applied to both small-site identity objects; it avoids choosing scheme pullback factorization maps to U_i.

If T is empty then every V→T has empty underlying space: a point of V would map to a point of T. On the etale site apply the open-cover criterion to the PEmpty-indexed family on V, whose joint-surjectivity condition is vacuous; its generated sieve is bottom. On the pro-etale site use Mathlib ProEt.bot_mem_topology on the empty domain. Apply these arguments also to V.left to obtain its small-site assertion. The slice assertion follows from the localized topology [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], since Sieve.overEquiv preserves bottom. Finally separatedness for the bottom covering sieve forces every pair of sections equal. The sectionwise-zero criterion from Step 4 then proves every module sheaf is zero. Empty and infinite index sets are allowed throughout.
